The parent component is re-rendering, and React re-renders all children by default — even with the same props. Three things cause this: **The props are new objects.** If you pass an inline function or object literal like `onClick={() => handleClick()}` or `style={{ color: 'red' }}`, it's a fresh reference every render, so React treats it as a different prop: ```jsx // Bad — new function every render handleClick()} /> // Good — function created once const handleChildClick = () => handleClick() ``` **The parent's state changed.** When the parent re-renders for any reason — its own state, props from above, context — React re-renders the child automatically. The props value doesn't matter. **You're not memoizing.** If the child genuinely receives the same props but you want to skip the render, wrap it in `React.memo`: ```jsx const Child = React.memo(({ name, value }) => { return
{name}: {value}
}) ``` This tells React to skip the render if the props haven't changed (by shallow equality). The fix depends on your situation: memoize inline functions and objects in the parent, or add `React.memo` to the child if props are truly identical. Check your browser DevTools Profiler tab — it shows which components re-rendered and why.
